result.topic_en: Euler introduces his method for finding very large primes by studying the divisors of numbers of the form aa+1, noting that such numbers admit only divisors that are themselves sums of two squares.
result.transcription:
204 DE NVMERIS PRIMIS
immenſi laboris. Quodſi autem quis forte hunc laborem ſuſciperet, certe non eſſet expectandum, vt vltra millionem a quoquam produceretur, eoque exantlato omnino impoſſibile videretur, vllum numerum primum exhibere, qui eſſet millione maior.

Occurrit autem mihi methodus peculiaris, ex qua per calculum non admodum taedioſum plures ſum adeptus numeros, non ſolum centies millibus, ſed etiam millione maiores, quos eſſe primos certo aſſeuerare poſſum. Quoniam igitur in tam ardua inueſtigatione leuiores ſucceſſus non ſunt contemnendi, haud inutile fore ſpero, ſi iſthanc methodum meam expoſuero, praeſertim cum ipſa ex proprietatibus numerorum non ſpernendis ſit deriuata, quae etiam in aliis inueſtigationibus vſum inſignem habere poſſe videntur.

Deductus autem ſum ad hanc methodum per conſiderationem numerorum quadratorum vnitate auctorum, ſeu in hac formula $aa+1$ contentorum, in quibus, ſiquidem $a$ ſit numerus par, plures numeros primos occurrere manifeſtum eſt, ſin autem $a$ ſit numerus impar, ſemiſſis illius formulae $\frac{1}{2}(aa+1)$ plurimos quoque ſuppeditat numeros primos. Quaeſiui ergo omnes diuiſores numerorum in hac forma $aa+1$ contentorum, qui labor non adeo erat taedioſus, cum non opus eſſet diuiſionem per omnes numeros primos radice $a$ minores tentare, propterea quod demonſtraui, atque id quidem poſt Fermatium, cuius autem demonſtratio pro deperdita eſt habenda, huiusmodi numeros $aa+1$ alios diuiſores non admittere, niſi qui ipſi
ſint

items.quote: plures ſum adeptus numeros, non ſolum centies millibus, ſed etiam millione maiores, quos eſſe primos certo aſſeuerare poſſum
items.english: I have obtained several numbers, not only greater than a hundred thousand but even greater than a million, which I can assert with certainty to be prime.

items.quote: haud inutile fore ſpero, ſi iſthanc methodum meam expoſuero
items.english: I hope it will not be useless if I expound this method of mine.

items.quote:
propterea quod demonſtraui, atque id quidem poſt Fermatium, cuius autem demonſtratio pro deperdita eſt habenda, huiusmodi numeros $aa+1$ alios diuiſores non admittere, niſi qui ipſi
ſint
items.english: because I have demonstrated (after Fermat, whose proof must be regarded as lost) that numbers of the form aa+1 admit no other divisors except those which are themselves [sums of two squares].
